issues.body: actions/checkout's pull_request default checks out refs/pull/N/merge, and this workflow explicitly documents that the suite grades that merge ref. Because github.event.pull_request.base.sha is an ancestor/parent of that synthetic HEAD, git merge-base HEAD $base returns $base itself. Thus mb_manifest duplicates base_manifest. For the target case where a self-test was added to base after the PR branch point, the required entry appears in this supposed merge-base manifest, so _derive_full_selftest_suite emits the old 'removed without approval' diagnosis. The marquee behavior therefore does not work in production despite the pure-function fixtures passing.
issues.fix_hint: Compute the merge base using github.event.pull_request.head.sha (validated/resolved fail-closed) and the base SHA, not checkout HEAD. Add a workflow-seam test that models the synthetic merge topology (base and PR head as the merge commit's two parents) and proves the selected manifest comes from the PR-head/base branch point rather than from the current base tip.
issues.title: Merge base is computed from the synthetic merge commit, not the PR head

verdict.summary: The new classifier is well exercised at the shell-function seam, but its production workflow supplies the wrong commit as the branch side of the merge-base calculation. This job intentionally checks out refs/pull/N/merge, so HEAD already contains the base commit. Consequently git merge-base HEAD $base resolves to $base, the generated merge-base manifest is just the current base manifest, and the behind-base condition this PR is meant to diagnose remains classified as a genuine removal. The workflow test pins the text of the faulty call but does not model the checkout topology, so it cannot catch this failure.
